name: NodeGraph
intent: Domain-neutral functional node graph: typed nodes and edges, a ZoomTools row (zoom in/out, editable percentage, fit, reset), selection by click or keyboard, node movement, optional edge creation, empty/loading/error states, and an inspector handoff for the current selection. The graph engine is an implementation detail — a consumer describes nodes rather than rendering them.
when: Pipeline or dataflow authoring where the steps are the content
A process lifecycle or state graph the user reads and rearranges
An analysis readiness or relationship graph with an evidence panel beside it
whenNot: A state machine with transition rules and guards -> use StateMachine, which carries that domain
A canvas whose nodes need bespoke rendering -> use GraphCanvas with your own nodeTypes
A hierarchy that reads better as a tree -> use TreeRow

chooseOver.component: GraphCanvas plus a hand-rolled node type and zoom chrome
chooseOver.because: GraphCanvas owns only the canvas chrome; every consumer then re-typed the node card, the zoom row, the selection plumbing and the loading/error states. This owns that contract, so four graphs share one visual language and no consumer types the engine's props.
The engine, its stylesheet and its version stay behind the widget; consumers describe nodes and edges instead of adopting a third-party API.

requiredProviders: None — it mounts its own graph context

nodes.note: id, label, and position; optional kind, description, status, tone, icon, footer, and the caller's data.

edges.note: id, source, target; optional label, tone, dashed, animated.

viewport.note: Controlled pan/zoom. With it the canvas stops framing itself.

dataContract.rowIdentity: Node and edge ids must be unique within one graph.

toolbar.description: Chrome on the left of the zoom row — a ContextToolbar, a filter, a legend

inspector.description: The evidence / detail handoff for the current selection; a right rail on desktop, stacked under the canvas below 1024px (so 820px stacks)

emptyAction.description: The action offered when the graph has no nodes

states.ready: The graph, with the zoom row live.
states.loading: Node-shaped skeletons; the zoom actions are parked.
states.error: The failure stated as a failure, with the host's Retry when it has one.
states.empty: The caller's empty title, description and action.
states.compact: Tighter node padding and type scale, for a graph with many nodes on screen.

allowedPlacement: inside a fixed-height or min-h-0 flex container
forbiddenPlacement: a container with no resolved height — the canvas collapses to a 0px strip
evaluationCriteria: A node's status reads through `tone`, not a colour class at the call site.
A tab-gated or lazy graph fetch passes `loading` / `error` rather than an empty node list.
Node positions the user drags are persisted through `onNodeMove` and passed back in `nodes`.
The graph sits in a container with a resolved height.

lineage.authoredBy: Core #204 — the catalogue gap found by the Connect product-contract migration (2026-09-09)

derivedFrom.source: The four Connect graph journeys that each rebuilt this on a raw engine: pipeline builder, process lifecycle, analysis readiness, product/evidence lineage
extracted: typed node/edge model with semantic tone
ZoomTools row: zoom in/out, editable percentage, fit, reset
selection by click and by keyboard, controlled or uncontrolled
node movement reported on drag stop

notes: Built on GraphCanvas, which stays the one door to @xyflow/react; this adds the contract above it and hides the engine from consumers (showControls={false}, because the zoom row owns those actions).
Reset is not Fit: Fit frames every node at whatever zoom fits, Reset returns to 100% centred — the scale the nodes were drawn for — or to defaultViewport when the host gave one.
Edge tone is applied as style.stroke rather than a stroke-* class: React Flow paints the path from --xy-edge-stroke, so a class on the edge group never reaches it.
The focus ring sits on the engine's node wrapper (via the node's className), because that — not the card inside it — is the element the browser focuses.
Dragged positions are held locally only until the incoming positions change, so a re-layout from the host always wins over a stale drag.

usage: Use NodeGraph to display structured data or visualizations. This component helps users understand and interact with complex information sets.

NodeGraph is ideal for dashboards, reports, and data-heavy interfaces. Ensure data is presented clearly and consider responsive behavior for different screen sizes. Provide appropriate loading states for async data.

props.name: layout
props.description: `layered` (default) wires a DAG with orthogonal edges; `free` suits a radial or hand-placed graph.

props.name: density
props.description: Row height and type scale. Default `comfortable`.

props.name: selectedNodeId
props.description: Controlled selection. Pass `null` for "nothing selected"; omit it entirely to stay uncontrolled.

props.name: selectable
props.description: Turn off node selection for the whole graph. Default true.

props.name: movable
props.description: Let nodes be dragged. Default true.

props.name: ...props
props.description: All standard HTML attributes are supported.

anatomy.description: NodeGraph is composed of the following parts:

bestPractices.title: Use semantic props
bestPractices.description: Use the component's built-in props rather than className overrides.

bestPractices.title: Don't override core styles
bestPractices.description: Avoid using className to override the component's fundamental styling.

bestPractices.title: Provide accessible labels
bestPractices.description: Include proper ARIA labels for screen reader users.

bestPractices.title: Don't skip accessibility
bestPractices.description: Never omit accessibility attributes for interactive components.

bestPractices.title: Handle all states
bestPractices.description: Account for loading, error, empty, and success states.

bestPractices.title: Don't ignore edge cases
bestPractices.description: Avoid showing broken UI when data is missing or loading.
